name: Tempester n°63 (from 1.6.7.0): the five Release parameters capped at 123 only while a Voice chip runs DSI's Voice OS; 127 when the six chips run Tempester Voice 1.5.1.0 (1.6.6.0 and older keep patch/release_cap.json)
explanation: Why: DSI's Voice OS never ends a release of 124-127 (R = T[r] >> 7 with no minimum, T[124..127] < 0x80); Tempester Voice 1.5.1.0 gives 101-127 a finite curve (up to 60 s at 127) in the five envelopes, Amp included, and answers 0xFE00 with 0x16 (DSI 0x15). So n°63's cap is lifted when, and only when, the six chips answered 0x16 at start-up; Amp Release (75), whose stock max of 123 came from the same endless release, reaches 127 too. Condition: main reads each chip's 0xFE00 reply once into the halfwords [address] (nothing else writes them); VOICE_CHECK (hook [address], right after the sixth read; it makes the replaced [routine](0xF500, 0) call as a tail jump) writes RELEASE_LIFT [address] (.bss hole, zero at start: capped) = 4 when the six words are 0x0016, else 0. n°63's three paths are gated by that byte, a lift of 0 giving 1.6.6.0's behaviour: the single-parameter sender [routine] (hook [address], CAP_WORD), the Timer 2 patch burst (hook [address], CAP_BURST, the test only in the five Release iterations) and the load validator [routine] (hook [address], CAP_LOAD: a Release above the table max becomes the effective max, 123 or 127, and a lifted 124-127 is kept). The table maxima stay 123 (flash constants, as 1.6.6.0); the three readers of the max that can see a Release add the lift to a max of 123 (among entries 0-159 only the five Releases have 123): the knob path [routine] (hook [address], MAX_KNOB; panel, CC, remote controls, NRPN), the value display [routine] (hook [address], MAX_DISPLAY) and n°9a's NRPN clamp (hook 0x9d07a24c, MAX_NRPN; the word is left out of patch/nrpn_reception_1670.json). [routine], [routine] and [routine] also read maxima, from the beat-wide list [address], which holds no Release; a reader missed would only keep 123. Code 0x9d07be00-0x9d07bfaf; RAM [address] (one byte). Proof: tools/sim_release_cap.py --lift and its counter-proofs. Source: release_cap_1670.s.
